Issues.Title: docs(router): use computed for fine-grained route resource params
Issues.Body:
The guide claimed that a route resource reading `ctx.queryParams()['category']` inside `params` does not refetch when an unrelated query parameter changes. This is not the case: `params` re-runs whenever `ctx.queryParams` changes, and the resource reloads even if the returned value is the same.

Show how to derive the value with `computed` instead, which only notifies when the value changes, and remove the incorrect tip about path params. Also add a router spec covering the documented pattern.

Fixes #71178

Issues.Title: docs: route resource params reading queryParams()['key'] inline still refetches on unrelated query changes (22.2.0)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

The guide says a resource that reads only ctx.queryParams()['category'] should not reload when another query key (e.g. sort) changes.
In @angular/router 22.2.0, this does not hold if the read is inline inside resource({ params }):
```
// Reloads when *any* query param changes (including `sort`)
byCategory: resource({
  params: () => ctx.queryParams()['category'] ?? 'all',
  loader: ({ params }) => api.fetchByCategory(params),
}),
```
`ctx.queryParams()` is one signal for the whole object. Any query change re-runs params, so the resource reloads even when 'category' is unchanged.

A workaround that actually worked for me:
```
const category = computed(() => ctx.queryParams()['category'] ?? 'all');

byCategory: resource({
  params: category,
  loader: ({ params }) => api.fetchByCategory(params),
}),
```

I have built a demo app where I experimented with all this new resource options, you'll find this use case there: https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/famzila/angular-route-resource-demo

### Enter the URL of the topic with the problem

https://angular.dev/guide/routing/data-fetching-with-resources#fine-grained-change-tracking-with-signals

Issues.Title: fix(forms): don't crash when formControlName has no matching control
Issues.Body:
Even tho reactive forms might be considered legacy now, this fix covers a real production case.

Prior to this commit, a `formControlName` with no control for it in the form group crashed in production with a raw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')`. The error said nothing about forms or which control was missing, so it was hard to trace back to the template. A common way to hit it: the template and the form group are built from the same list but with two different filters, so an item passes the template's filter but was never given a control.

`AbstractFormDirective.addControl` read `this.form.get(dir.path)` and passed the result into `_setupWithForm` without a null check. In dev mode this was still caught earlier, in `setUpControlValueAccessor` ("Cannot find control with path"). In production `ngDevMode` strips that check away, so the null control reached `setUpValidators`, which dereferences it right away and threw the bare `TypeError`.

With this fix, `addControl` checks the control first and throws a coded `RuntimeError` (NG01055), with a docs page on angular.dev. The check is not gated behind `ngDevMode`, since the crash it prevents is a production one. The message stays `ngDevMode`-only and lists the sibling controls that exist at that path, which is usually enough to spot a name mismatch.

Fixes #71155
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(forms): don't crash when formControlName has no matching control" (#71177)

Issues.Title: fix(router): check abort signal state on subscribe
Issues.Body:
Prior to this commit, `abortSignalToObservable` checked `signal.aborted` when the observable was created, not when it was subscribed. canMatch and canLoad guards create their observables first and subscribe to them later, so a guard that starts a new navigation (e.g. calls `router.navigateByUrl()` and returns `false`) could abort the signal in between. Earlier guards then added the abort listener to an already aborted signal, never saw the abort and stayed subscribed until they settled on their own (or forever, if they never emit). There's no open issue for this, likely because people don't see router internals and might expect earlier guards to keep running as normal behavior.

With this fix, the aborted state is checked on subscribe, so earlier guards are never subscribed once the navigation has been aborted.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(router): check abort signal state on subscribe" (#71176)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): ignore `@let` declarations in the control flow content projection diagnostic
Issues.Body: ## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? NG8011 fires when a `@let` declaration sits next to the node at the root of a control flow block: ```html @if (hasError()) { @let message = 'Email is required'; {{ message }} } ``` The warning says `` won't be projected into the `[error]` slot, but it is. Since #58607 the compiler skips `@let` declarations when it looks for the single root node of a block. The diagnostic does its own count in `TcbControlFlowContentProjectionOp.shouldCheck` and still treats the `@let` as a second root node. Issue Number: Fixes #71172 ## What is the new behavior? `shouldCheck` skips `@let` declarations, so the diagnostic agrees with what the compiler does. I added two tests: one for the case above (no diagnostic), and one with a `@let` plus a stray text node, which is still reported. The first one fails without the change. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information It only removes a false-positive warning; the generated code doesn't change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): ignore `@let` declarations in the control flow content projection diagnostic" (#71173)

Issues.Title: fix(forms): throw a coded error for missing controls in production
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The missing control checks in `setUpControlValueAccessor` and `setUpFormContainer` only run in development mode. When a template contains a `formControlName` for a control the `FormGroup` does not have, development builds report `Cannot find control with path: 'Options -> 2'`, but production builds strip the check, the `null` control reaches `setUpValidators`, and the application crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')`, which gives no indication that a form control path failed to resolve.

Issue Number: #71155

## What is the new behavior?

Both functions throw a `RuntimeError` with the existing `MISSING_CONTROL` code in all build modes. Production builds now report `NG01001: Cannot find control with path: '...'` instead of the bare `TypeError`, and development builds keep the same message text, now prefixed with the code.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

The affected configurations already crash in production; the change only replaces the crash with a coded error that identifies the failing control location. Error type changes from `TypeError` to `RuntimeError`, which both extend `Error`.

## Other information

The new test simulates production by setting `ngDevMode` to `false` and asserts the coded error for `formGroup.addControl` with an unresolvable path, mirroring the existing development mode assertion next to it.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(forms): throw a coded error for missing controls in production" (#71171)

Issues.Title: fix(core): sanitize href bindings on SVG image elements
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The DOM security schema registers a URL security context for the `href` and `xlink:href` attributes of `svg:a`, but not for the SVG image loading elements `svg:image` and `svg:feImage`. Bindings on those elements reach the DOM without sanitization, and values marked trusted through `DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustUrl` cannot be used with them: an attribute binding stringifies the wrapper instead of unwrapping it, which produces an attribute value that starts with `SafeValue must use [property]=binding` and no image is loaded.

Issue Number: #38854

## What is the new behavior?

`href` and `xlink:href` bindings on `svg:image` and `svg:feImage` are sanitized with the URL security context, matching the existing handling of `img[src]` and `svg:a[href]`. Untrusted values are passed through `_sanitizeUrl`, so only `javascript:` URLs are prefixed with `unsafe:` and every other scheme, including custom application schemes and `data:` URIs, is passed through unchanged. Trusted values created with `bypassSecurityTrustUrl` are unwrapped and bound as-is, which is what the issue reporter needs for the `app://` scheme used in their Cordova setup.

Because both the schema for the SVG namespace and the defensive lookup for elements without an explicit namespace live in `checkSecurityContext`, an `image` or `feImage` element that appears without an SVG namespace is now also sanitized. This mirrors how the SVG animation attributes are treated and is strictly a tightening: values that previously passed through raw continue to pass through unless they start with `javascript:`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

An application would only observe a difference when binding a `javascript:` URL to `href` or `xlink:href` on an SVG `image` or `feImage` element, which is not a working image source in any browser. Values marked with `bypassSecurityTrustHtml` or another mismatched trust type were already rejected.

## Other information

Both copies of the schema (`packages/compiler/src/schema/dom_security_schema.ts` and `packages/core/src/sanitization/dom_security_schema.ts`) are updated, along with schema registry tests, runtime sanitization unit tests, and template integration tests that cover sanitization and trusted value unwrapping.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): sanitize href bindings on SVG image elements" (#71167)

Issues.Title: fix(http): allow an empty string as a mapped origin value
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`mapRequestOriginUrl` uses a falsy check to detect whether an entry exists in `HTTP_TRANSFER_CACHE_ORIGIN_MAP`, so an empty string value is treated as if no mapping was configured. In addition, `verifyMappedOrigin` rejects the empty string because parsing it against the dummy base URL produces an empty pathname rather than a slash. An application that reaches its API without an origin prefix on the client therefore cannot express its mapping at all.

Issue Number: #58149

## What is the new behavior?

Only an `undefined` entry is treated as absent, and the empty string is accepted as a mapping that rewrites the request URL to a root-relative path. A response cached on the server for `http://internal-domain.com:1234/test-1?foo=1` with the mapping `{'http://internal-domain.com:1234': ''}` is now reused on the client for the request `/test-1?foo=1`. The token documentation describes the empty string form.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Configurations that already work keep working: non-empty origins follow the same code path as before, and a missing entry still means no mapping.

## Other information

The new test mirrors the existing "cache with public origin" coverage and also runs the development mode verification path, which is where the empty string was previously rejected.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(http): allow an empty string as a mapped origin value" (#71168)

Issues.Title: fix(router): skip dot segments in any part of the first command
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When `computeNavigation` splits the first command string on slashes, only a dot part at index zero is skipped. A dot part at any later position is pushed as a literal segment, so `router.navigate(['./segment/./segment'])` or a `routerLink` with the same value produces a `UrlTree` that contains a `.` path segment. Route matching then fails with `Cannot match any routes`, even though a browser strips the dot segments when the same URL is entered in the address bar, because browsers normalize dot segments per RFC 3986 before the router ever sees the URL.

Issue Number: #27929

## What is the new behavior?

Every single dot part of the first command is skipped, not only the leading one. `./segment/./segment` now resolves to the same tree as `./segment/segment`. This mirrors the existing handling of `..`, which already counts at any position of the first command.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

The only observable difference is that first commands containing inner dot parts no longer produce a `.` path segment. Such a segment cannot match any sensible route configuration today, so navigations that previously failed now succeed. Commands passed as separate array elements are untouched, including the ones the existing security tests rely on to exercise the protocol-relative serialization fallback, which keeps working as before.

## Other information

The scope is deliberately limited to command parsing in `createUrlTree`, which is the path used by `Router.navigate`, `RouterLink`, and `ActivatedRoute.createUrlTree`. The URL serializer that parses whole URL strings is left unchanged because it is also used to parse `redirectTo` values, where dot segments carry relative redirect semantics.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(router): skip dot segments in any part of the first command" (#71170)

Issues.Title: fix(service-worker): fall back on the network when assigning a version fails
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`Driver#handleFetch()` awaits `assignVersion()` without protecting against its failure. Persisting a new client assignment goes through `sync()`, which writes to storage, and when that write fails (typically a quota error) the exception rejects the `respondWith()` promise of the very request that triggered it. The client then gets a failed response for its navigation, and since every new client repeats the failing assignment on its first request, the application stays broken until the service worker state is cleared.

Issue Number: #36086

## What is the new behavior?

A failure while assigning a version is caught and logged through the debugger, and the request continues without an assigned version, which makes it fall back on the network through the existing `safeFetch()` path. Clients that already have an assignment keep being served from their cached version, and only the request whose assignment could not be persisted pays the network cost.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

The change only converts a rejected response into a network response for requests whose version assignment could not be persisted.

## Other information

This is the narrowly scoped handling that was discussed in the previous attempt on this issue: only the `assignVersion()` call inside `handleFetch()` is guarded, leaving all other `CacheTable#write()` paths untouched, since those are either already handled or surface through the degraded mode machinery. The new test makes cache writes throw after initialization and verifies that a request from a new client still receives a response from the server.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(service-worker): fall back on the network when assigning a version fails" (#71169)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): match namespaced root nodes of control flow blocks against ng-content tag selectors
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When an `<svg>` or `<math>` element is the only root node of an `@if`, `@for` or `@switch` branch, it isn't projected into an `ng-content` slot with a tag selector such as `select="svg"`. It goes to the default slot instead. The compiler passes the root's tag name to `ɵɵconditionalCreate` / `ɵɵrepeaterCreate` with its namespace prefix (`":svg:svg"`), so the runtime never matches it against `svg`.

Issue Number: Fixes #71162

## What is the new behavior?

The namespace prefix is stripped in `ingestControlFlowInsertionPoint`, the same way it already is for regular elements and structural templates, so the generated tag name is `"svg"` / `"math"` and the block lands in the right slot.

I added acceptance tests for `@if`/`@else`, `@for`/`@empty` and `@switch` with SVG and MathML roots, plus one with an `<svg *ngIf>` root since that goes through the template branch of the same code. There's also a compliance test that checks the emitted tag names and that the branch templates still call `ɵɵnamespaceSVG`/`ɵɵnamespaceMathML`. Without the change in `ingest.ts`, all six new tests fail.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Strictly speaking, apps that rely on the current behavior (an `<svg>` root inside a control flow block ending up in the default slot next to a `select="svg"` slot) will see it move to the `svg` slot, which is where it would go without the control flow block. The workaround people may have used, `ngProjectAs="svg"`, keeps working.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): match namespaced root nodes of control flow blocks against ng-content tag selectors" (#71163)

Issues.Title: Support [disabled] attribute on [formField] inputs
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

forms

### Description

Using [formField] removes support for angular and native (attr.) bindings for things like disabled, required, etc. I can work around the lack of required thanks to validateStandardSchema and using requiredness from something like zod for reusability. Disabled however, appears to be forced to do something like `disabled(...)` in the form schema management which I despise as a pattern.

It is often the case that forms of any complexity and/or using components across multiple forms should not have to copy/paste a block of disabled, required, etc. logic. Previously, it's encapsulated in the child component that knows how its inputs should be managed.

For example, in a child component - a checkbox that disables a sibling input. In this new world, I'd have to do something like tie the checkbox value into the form value for exposure at the root form schema level so the child component's path can disable the appropriate input. Then, if this is used in another form, I have to do the exact same thing and so on. Additionally, if that condition ever changes, I have to update X forms worth of disabled logic. Instead of being able to modularly define my component management, it's now all top loaded at each form level which is not maintainable (not to mention having to *find* each form that uses the respective path associated to said component).


### Proposed solution

I would like inputs to once again support [disabled] (and optionally other things like required, if for no reason other than consistency) while using [formField]. If the [disabled] value needs to be a (writable?) signal instead of a primitive so that you can facilitate automatically changing the [formField] disabled value and viceversa to the [disabled] value, I can live with that.

I suppose I could also live with just an easy way to programmatically set disabled on the fieldState via an effect although I think this is less than ideal since now we have to individually manage a lot of side effects that should be unnecessary.

### Alternatives considered

An alternative to this could in theory be a function per child component that encapsulates all the relevant logic (taking a partial form schema as an argument) but that's a lot more boilerplate that should absolutely not be necessary and also beings to become quite unmaintainable at scale when there are lots of adapter child components around various inputs.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Support [disabled] attribute on [formField] inputs" (#71160)

Issues.Title: Reactive Forms: formControlName with no matching control crashes in production with a raw TypeError
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

If the template renders a `formControlName` for a control that the `FormGroup` doesn't have, the error depends on the build:

- **Dev mode:** `Error: Cannot find control with path: 'Options -> 2'`, which is clear.
- **Production:** `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')`. It says nothing about forms or which control is missing, so it is hard to trace back to the template.

A real-world way to hit this: the template and the `FormGroup` are built from the same list but with two different filters. An item passes the template's filter but not the form's, so the template asks for a control that was never added.

Cause: `AbstractFormDirective.addControl()` passes the result of `this.form.get(dir.path)` on without checking it for `null`. In dev mode, a `ngDevMode`-only check in `setUpControlValueAccessor` catches it. That check is stripped from production builds, so the `null` control reaches `setUpValidators`, which uses it right away.

Expected: a clear, coded error in production too, instead of a bare `TypeError`.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/arturovt/form-control-name-missing-control-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
Production build:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')

Dev build:
```

Issues.Title: fix(forms): handle standard schema issues whose path runs through unknown keys
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`standardIssueToFormTreeError()` walks a Standard Schema issue's path with `target = target[pathKey]`. When the last key is unknown to the model, `target` ends up `undefined` and the error falls back to the field being validated. When a key **before** the last one is unknown, the next step reads a property of `undefined` and `errors()` throws:

```ts
form(signal({name: ''}), (p) =>
  validateStandardSchema(p, z.object({name: z.string()}).superRefine((_, ctx) => {
    ctx.addIssue({code: 'custom', message: 'Wrong.', path: ['ghost', 'name']});
  })),
)().errors();
// TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')
```

Issue Number: #71128

## What is the new behavior?

The path walk stops descending once it leaves the model (`target?.[pathKey]`), so the issue is reported on the field being validated, the same fallback that already applies when only the last key is unknown.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Added two tests to `packages/forms/signals/test/node/api/validators/standard_schema.spec.ts`: one for an unknown last key (existing behavior) and one for a path that runs through an unknown key. `//packages/forms/signals/test/node:test` passes locally (543 specs); without the fix the new test fails with the `TypeError` above.

An alternative would be to report the issue on the deepest existing field instead of the validated field. I kept the existing fallback for consistency, but happy to change it if preferred.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): do not scope nested compound selectors starting with `&`
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Since d0d7f57e08 (#69885) nested rules are scoped, which also appends the content attribute to compound selectors starting with `&`. Under `:host`, `&` refers to the host element, which only carries the `_nghost-*` attribute, so the rule silently stops matching (regression in 22.2.0):

```css
/* input */
:host { display: block; &.md { width: 70px; } }

/* 22.1.8 */
[_nghost-c1] { display: block; &.md { width: 70px; } }

/* 22.2.0 */
[_nghost-c1] { display: block; &.md[_ngcontent-c1] { width: 70px; } }
```

Issue Number: #71050

## What is the new behavior?

A compound selector starting with `&` (e.g. `&.md`, `&:hover`, `&[attr]`) is left unscoped, because it can only match elements already matched by the scoped parent selector. Descendants are still scoped:

```css
:host { &.md {} & .child {} &.md > .child {} }
/* => */
[a-host] { &.md {} & .child[contenta] {} &.md > .child[contenta] {} }
```

This also covers `:host(.foo)` and `:host-context(.foo)` parents. For non-host parents (e.g. `.parent { &.modifier {} }`) the output changes from `&.modifier[contenta]` to `&.modifier`, which matches the same elements since `&` already resolves to `.parent[contenta]`. The two existing expectations in `nesting_spec.ts` were updated accordingly. Selectors that only reference `&` inside a pseudo-class (e.g. `.a:not(&)`) are still scoped.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

New tests added to `packages/compiler/test/shadow_css/nesting_spec.ts` for `:host`, `:host(.foo)`, `:host-context(.foo)` and descendants of `&`. They fail without the change and pass with it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): do not scope nested compound selectors starting with `&`" (#71152)

Issues.Title: serve: with NG_HMR_CSTYLES=1, component stylesheets not touched by the last change revert to first-build content after a rebuild
Issues.Body: ### Command serve ### Is this a regression? Unknown. I have only tested 22.2.1. ### Description With `NG_HMR_CSTYLES=1` (link-based component style hot reloading), `ng serve` emits component stylesheets as external `/.css?ngcomp=...` links. After a rebuild, the dev server serves fresh content only for the stylesheet(s) affected by that change. Every other component stylesheet is served with its content from the first build, dropping earlier edits that are still saved on disk. Each check below is a fresh request for the page and its `?ngcomp` links, so a freshly loaded page receives the stale content too. Without the flag, the same edit sequence (steps c1 to c5) produces no stale stylesheet. Hypothesis (unverified, from reading the code, not from debugging): in `@angular/build/src/builders/application/execute-build.js`, on every rebuild with `externalRuntimeStyles` the code runs ```js // TODO: Only attempt rebundling of invalidated styles once incremental build results are supported. if (rebuildState && options.externalRuntimeStyles) { componentStyleBundler.invalidate(rebuildState.fileChanges.all); const componentResults = await componentStyleBundler.bundleAllFiles(true, true); bundlingIndividualResults.push(...componentResults); } ``` so only the invalidated sheets are re-bundled, and the sheets that are not invalidated seem to be served from their initial-build output rather than their last-built output. I have not confirmed which layer (bundler cache, result merging, or the dev server asset map) drops the later content. Side observation, no claim about impact: with the flag, the SSR HTML contains no inline `
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "serve: with NG_HMR_CSTYLES=1, component stylesheets not touched by the last change revert to first-build content after a rebuild" (#34248)

Issues.Title: dev-server on macOS misses changes outside the workspace root: one FSEvents stream per external directory exceeds the per-process limit
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

21.2.24 (watchpack)

### Description

`ParcelExternalManager.ensureDirWatched` (packages/angular/build/src/utils/watcher.ts) calls `parcelWatcher.subscribe()` once per directory outside the workspace root. On macOS every subscription is its own FSEvents stream, and macOS refuses to start more than about 512 streams per process (parcel-bundler/watcher#190). The rejection is caught and ignored ("Ignore subscription errors for missing or restricted external directories"), so the files in those directories are silently not watched and editing them never triggers a rebuild.

Our setup: npm workspaces monorepo; the Angular workspace (angular.json) lives in `<monorepo>/apps/<APP>` and the app imports ~100 libraries from `<monorepo>/libs/*` through tsconfig paths. One `ng serve` registers 1,278 external directories (about 1,000 library source folders plus 274 node_modules packages). Instrumenting the `catch` in `ensureDirWatched` on 22.2.1 (which already contains #34187):

- 1,278 subscribe attempts
- 511 succeed
- 767 fail with `Error starting FSEvents stream`

Which directories end up watched depends on subscription order. I edited 22 files in one batch with `ng serve --verbose`: 1 app file, 11 library files in directories whose subscription succeeded, and 10 in directories whose subscription failed. The 12 in watched directories show up in the modified list and rebuild; the 10 others never do (waited 150 s).

### Minimal Reproduction

Any workspace whose app compiles sources from more than ~510 directories outside the workspace root, on macOS:

1. Create a workspace in `apps/app` and ~600 small libraries in `libs/lib-N/src/index.ts`, mapped through tsconfig `paths` and all imported by the app.
2. `ng serve --verbose`.
3. Edit `libs/lib-599/src/index.ts`: no rebuild. Edit `libs/lib-1/src/index.ts`: rebuild (or the other way around, depending on subscription order).

The limit itself reproduces with @parcel/watcher alone (script in parcel-bundler/watcher#190: subscribing 1,000 sibling folders fails from about 500 on with `Error starting FSEvents stream`).

### Exception or Error

```text
Nothing is printed. The error is swallowed in ensureDirWatched; with an instrumented catch every failing subscription rejects with:

Error: Error starting FSEvents stream
```

### Your Environment

```text
@angular/build 22.2.1 (22.3.0-next.0 has the same ParcelExternalManager)
@angular/cli 22.2.1
@angular/core 22.2.1
@parcel/watcher 2.6.0
Node.js 24.21.0
npm 11.19
macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon
```

### Anything else relevant?

Workarounds measured on the same project with the same 22 edits; idle CPU is the dev-server process tree over 60 s:

| Variant | Streams | Edits detected | Idle CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22.2.1 as shipped | 511 ok / 767 failed | 12/22 | 0.1 % |
| `NG_BUILD_WATCH_ROOT=1` | 511 ok / 767 failed | 12/22 | n/a |
| `--poll 2500` | chokidar | 22/22 | 22.9 % of a core |
| `--poll 1000` | chokidar | 22/22 | 46.9 % of a core |
| local patch: subscribe the common ancestor of the external directory and the workspace root | 2 ok / 0 failed | 22/22 | 0.1 % |

Suggested fix: avoid one stream per directory on macOS, for example by subscribing a common ancestor (VS Code does the same, see the discussion in parcel-bundler/watcher#190), or by falling back to an ancestor subscription when `subscribe` rejects. At minimum, log the swallowed error in verbose mode so the problem is visible.

On 21.2.24 (watchpack) edits to these library files rebuilt reliably.

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): immediately purge freed rolldown arena memory
Issues.Body:
Rolldown's native binding statically links mimalloc v3, which defaults to a 4-second arena purge delay (MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=1000 * MIMALLOC_ARENA_PURGE_MULT=4) and only executes scheduled purges cooperatively during subsequent allocations. In single-run CLI builds where Rolldown is not invoked again after bundling completes, non-zero purge delays prevent freed arena pages from being returned to the OS, increasing peak RSS when subsequent post-bundle stages run.

Introduce a shared loadRolldown() helper used by both the application chunk optimizer and the library builder that temporarily sets MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 (when not already configured in the environment) while loading Rolldown's native binding so mimalloc caches a 0ms purge delay without leaving the variable set in process.env.

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/main/pnpm) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.6.0` → `12.8.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.6.0/12.8.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.8.1?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/12.8.1?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/12.6.0/12.8.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.6.0/12.8.1?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.8.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.8.1): pnpm 12.8.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/pnpm@12.8.0...v12.8.1) pnpm 12.8.1 fixes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting lockfiles with injected workspace packages that have peers, restores the executable bit on files of local directory dependencies, makes `pnpm dedupe` converge, and uses less CPU on many-core machines. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​16332](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16332). - Executable files in a `file:` directory dependency or an injected workspace package keep their executable bit again. Since 12.8.0, pnpm installed these files without the permissions they have in their project. - `pnpm dedupe` now reaches a stable lockfile when a package's peer suffix is long enough to be hashed. Before, each run could switch that package's key between the hashed and the spelled-out suffix, so `pnpm dedupe --check` always failed [#​16331](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16331). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the default in CI, now uses less CPU on machines with more than 8 cores. Warm installs on many-core Windows machines got up to 10% faster. Frozen installs now link with at most 16 worker threads. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as outdated after a filtered install just because `pnpm-lock.yaml` has a newer modification time. It checks the lockfile against the packages that install put in place. Before, `pnpm run` reinstalled the whole workspace with lifecycle scripts on, for example after a Docker `COPY` brought in a lockfile with a newer mtime [#​16322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16322). After a filtered install, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now also checks that the install put the selected projects' dependencies in place. A `node_modules` directory alone no longer counts as proof. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer install a project that has never been installed and has nothing to install. Such a project declares no dependencies, no peer dependencies that `autoInstallPeers` would fetch, and no install lifecycle scripts. The command now runs without writing `node_modules` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​16313](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16313). - `pnpm update -g --latest` now upgrades globally installed packages beyond their saved version ranges [#​16320](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16320). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.8.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.8.0): pnpm 12.8 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.7.0...pnpm@12.8.0) pnpm 12.8.0 warns when `pnpm pack` or `pnpm publish` would ship a `.env` file that `files` does not list, installs `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` workspaces concurrently, applies every setting passed as `--config.=`, and no longer leaves the Windows terminal stuck after Ctrl+C in a script. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now warn when the tarball includes a `.env` or `.env.*` file that the `files` field of `package.json` does not list. Templates such as `.env.example` are not reported. List the file in `files` to publish it on purpose, or exclude it in `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` [#​7826](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7826). - `pnpm pack` now honors `--silent`, `--reporter=silent`, and `--loglevel=silent` to hide the tarball contents and summary. With `--json`, lifecycle script output and the final JSON output remain visible [#​10297](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10297). ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - Installing through a `pnpr` server now records the pnpmfile checksum in the lockfile, so a later `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts that lockfile [#​14460](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14460). A frozen install through the pnpr server now fails if the pnpmfile changed. If the pnpmfile defines a `readPackage`, `afterAllResolved` or `preResolution` hook or custom resolvers, pnpm resolves dependencies locally and prints a warning that the pnpr server was not used. Installing through a `pnpr` server also links a workspace project at the directory its `publishConfig.directory` names. A server that does not forward the setting makes the install fail with `ERR_PNPM_PNPR_PUBLISH_DIRECTORY_MISMATCH`, so pnpm never writes a lockfile that points at the wrong directory. The server rejects a `publishConfig.directory` that points outside its project. - Installing a git-hosted dependency that has to be built no longer fails when that dependency's own dependencies have build scripts nobody approved. pnpm skips those builds while preparing the dependency, as it does without `strictDepBuilds` [#​9764](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9764). - A git-hosted dependency that is a pnpm workspace with no committed lockfile is now detected as a pnpm project [#​14011](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14011). - `pnpm install --dev` and `pnpm fetch --dev` now install the optional dependencies of devDependencies, such as the platform binaries of Biome and oxlint. The project's own `optionalDependencies` are still skipped [#​9678](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9678). - `pnpm install --offline` and `pnpm add --offline` now resolve a version range to the newest matching version whose tarball is already in the store. They used to pick the newest version in the cached metadata and fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL` when its tarball was missing [#​10715](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10715). - If an offline install fails because the registry metadata cache uses the layout from before pnpm 11.27 and 12.4, the error now names the older mirror on disk and explains that one online install repopulates the cache. Before, `cmd` expanded `%VAR%` in them and backslashes arrived doubled. Line breaks still arrive as the two characters `\n`, because `cmd` cannot pass them. The command line pnpm prints for the script quotes the arguments the same way on every platform [#​16257](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16257). - The Windows `pnpm.exe` runs on a clean Windows install that does not have the Visual C++ Redistributable. It used to exit immediately on startup because that runtime was missing [#​15723](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15723). - On Windows, the `.cmd` command shims in `node_modules/.bin` now keep a `%` in the project path. Before, cmd.exe expanded it as a variable reference, so the command received a mangled `NODE_PATH` [#​15716](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15716). Command shims also run tools whose paths contain non-ASCII characters [#​6999](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6999), including the PowerShell shims in Windows PowerShell 5.1 [#​16217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16217). - Bin shims in `node_modules/.bin` run from Cygwin on Windows again. The shims passed a `/cygdrive/c/...` path to the Windows `node` found on `PATH`, so Node.js failed with `Cannot find module 'C:\cygdrive\c\...'` [#​12845](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12845). - On Windows, installing pnpm with npm inside a project now writes `node_modules/.bin` shims that run `pnpm.exe`. A global install with `npm install --location=global` now gets the same shims as `npm install -g` [#​15688](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15688). - `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_WORKSPACE_INVALID_GLOB` on Windows for a wildcard pattern such as `plugins/*/*` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the workspace is on a different drive than the pnpm cache or state directory [#​16239](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16239). - On Windows, `pnpm install` no longer skips a dependency's build script on a later install when the package ships an executable file and the script changes nothing inside the package directory [#​15667](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15667). - `pnpm setup` no longer writes the `pn.ps1`, `pnpx.ps1`, and `pnx.ps1` PowerShell wrappers. It also removes the ones an earlier setup wrote. PowerShell now runs `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` through their `.cmd` wrappers, like `pnpm` itself. Before, these aliases failed with a "not digitally signed" error wherever the execution policy blocks unsigned scripts [#​8444](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8444). - `pnpm setup` on Windows no longer panics when an unrelated environment variable has a name containing a non-ASCII character. It skips that variable [#​15684](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15684). - On Windows, `pnpm setup` repairs the `PNPM_HOME` registry type left by older pnpm versions, even when the configured directory has not changed. - On Windows, the `ERR_PNPM_BAD_ENV_FOUND` error of `pnpm setup` now shows the value `PNPM_HOME` is currently set to. Before, it showed the directory pnpm wanted to set. - On Windows, pnpm expands nested `%VAR%` references in `PNPM_HOME` and the other directory environment variables it uses for its home, store, cache, state, and config directories. pnpm fails with an error when a `%VAR%` reference remains after expansion [#​13236](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13236). - On Windows, if the global bin directory is not in `PATH` and a `PATH` entry still contains an unexpanded variable such as `%PNPM_HOME%`, the error now names that entry. A variable referenced from the user `Path` must be set to a full path and stored as a plain string (`REG_SZ`) for the entry to expand [#​5283](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5283). ##### Inspecting dependencies - `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit signatures` now fail with an error when the lockfile contains unresolvable dependency references [#​13638](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13638). - `pnpm licenses list` now reports the actual on-disk package locations when using `nodeLinker: hoisted` or `shamefully-hoist: true` [#​8589](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8589). With `--json`, its `paths` array now includes every installed copy of a package, including hoisted copies and isolated installations with different peer dependencies. - `pnpm root` now prints the configured `modulesDir`. It used to print `node_modules` regardless of the setting. A project's own `modulesDir` from `packageConfigs` is printed too [#​9113](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9113). ##### Output and messages - With the default and append-only reporters, installs with `--loglevel warn` or `--loglevel error` now print the full output of a failed install script. The output of successful scripts, including the root project's own install hooks, stays hidden. With `--loglevel warn`, pnpm also prints ignored build script warnings. - When a dependency fails to resolve, the error now shows the cause. For example, a Node.js runtime download behind a proxy that re-signs TLS now reports `invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer` [#​9556](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9556). - When installing a git dependency over SSH fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`, pnpm suggests checking the loaded keys with `ssh-add -l`. Resolving an SSH URL that refuses the key also shows a local HTTPS rewrite that leaves the recorded URL alone [#​13743](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13743). - Lockfile verification now fails with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_URL_MISMATCH`, `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_REVISION_MISMATCH`, or `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_NAMED_REGISTRY` when every rejected entry failed that check. These failures were reported as the generic `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_RESOLUTION_VERIFICATION`. - The lockfile verification error now suggests relaxing the policy that flagged an entry only if a fresh resolution still fails and you trust the affected packages. Errors from checks that no policy controls, such as a missing tarball integrity, no longer suggest relaxing a policy [#​14411](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14411). - `pnpm install` no longer prints an extra `Progress:` line after the progress line is marked `done` [#​16184](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16184). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.7.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.7.0): pnpm 12.7 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.6.0...v12.7.0) pnpm 12.7.0 ships with `.nvmrc` and `.node-version` support in the global `node` shim, `pnpm install --allow-build`, `pnpm publish --publish-wait-timeout`, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` created from the `workspaces` field. `pnpm install --force` no longer installs optional dependencies built for other platforms. This release also carries security fixes for bin shims on Nix, for lifecycle scripts of packages in a `storeDir` inside the workspace, and for `userAgent` placeholders in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm install --force` now keeps skipping optional dependencies whose `os`, `cpu` or `libc` do not match the host. It still refetches every package and lifts `engineStrict`. The new `forceIgnoresPlatform` setting restores the previous behaviour, installing optional dependencies of every platform under `--force` [#​6133](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6133). - The global `node` shim created by pnpm now uses the Node.js version from the nearest `.nvmrc` or `.node-version` file when the project does not declare a Node.js runtime in `devEngines.runtime` or `engines.runtime` [#​4471](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/4471). The nearest directory with a Node.js runtime declaration decides the version. Within one directory, `package.json` takes precedence over `.node-version`, which takes precedence over `.nvmrc`. An `.nvmrc` value that only nvm can act on, such as `system` or a custom alias, is ignored. - `pnpm install` now supports the `--allow-build` option to selectively allow or deny package lifecycle scripts and record them in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​15388](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15388). - Added `pnpm publish --publish-wait-timeout ` to wait for published versions and their tarballs to become available from the registry. Set `publishWaitTimeout` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to configure a default. A value of `0` disables the check. Recursive publishing confirms availability before publishing dependent packages. If confirmation times out, the command fails. When `pnpm publish -r --report-summary` fails after some uploads were accepted, the summary file now lists those packages. - `pnpm install` now creates `pnpm-workspace.yaml` from the `workspaces` field of the root `package.json` when the repository has no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. The projects the field lists are linked on that same install. An existing `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is never changed. With `--ignore-workspace`, no file is created. If the `workspaces` field later differs from `packages` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, pnpm prints a warning [#​2255](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2255). - When a project pins a pnpm version or a runtime that another pnpm process is installing at that moment, pnpm now waits a few seconds and then installs and runs a private copy of its own. It used to wait up to five minutes and then use the shared install directory without the lock. The private copy is removed once the command has run. `pnpm store prune` removes any private copy that a killed process left behind [#​15413](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15413). - pnp > ❗ **Important** > > ✂ PR body was truncated to here.

### [`v12.8.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.8.1): pnpm 12.8.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/pnpm@12.8.0...v12.8.1)

pnpm 12.8.1 fixes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting lockfiles with injected workspace packages that have peers, restores the executable bit on files of local directory dependencies, makes `pnpm dedupe` converge, and uses less CPU on many-core machines.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​16332](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16332).

- Executable files in a `file:` directory dependency or an injected workspace package keep their executable bit again. Since 12.8.0, pnpm installed these files without the permissions they have in their project.

- `pnpm dedupe` now reaches a stable lockfile when a package's peer suffix is long enough to be hashed. Before, each run could switch that package's key between the hashed and the spelled-out suffix, so `pnpm dedupe --check` always failed [#​16331](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16331).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the default in CI, now uses less CPU on machines with more than 8 cores. Warm installs on many-core Windows machines got up to 10% faster. Frozen installs now link with at most 16 worker threads.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as outdated after a filtered install just because `pnpm-lock.yaml` has a newer modification time. It checks the lockfile against the packages that install put in place. Before, `pnpm run` reinstalled the whole workspace with lifecycle scripts on, for example after a Docker `COPY` brought in a lockfile with a newer mtime [#​16322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16322).

  After a filtered install, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now also checks that the install put the selected projects' dependencies in place. A `node_modules` directory alone no longer counts as proof.

- `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer install a project that has never been installed and has nothing to install. Such a project declares no dependencies, no peer dependencies that `autoInstallPeers` would fetch, and no install lifecycle scripts. The command now runs without writing `node_modules` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​16313](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16313).

- `pnpm update -g --latest` now upgrades globally installed packages beyond their saved version ranges [#​16320](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16320).
